issue.title: Make group info screen scrollable for long member lists

<summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@lib/providers/auth_provider.dart`:
- Around line 229-241: In _completeLogin, avoid emitting the full stable
identifier account.pubkey to logs: keep writing the full pubkey to secure
storage (storage.write with _storageKey and state = AsyncData(account.pubkey))
but change the _logger.info call to log a redacted preview or non-identifying
state instead (e.g., account.accountType or a short preview like first/last 6
chars or a hash of account.pubkey) so the unique pubkey value is not stored in
app logs; update the message passed to _logger.info accordingly and ensure the
change only affects the log text around _logger.info in _completeLogin.

In `@lib/services/external_signer_callback_registry.dart`:
- Around line 8-22: ExternalSignerCallbackRegistry currently holds mutable
process state in _registeredExternalSignerPubkeys and
_externalSignerRegistrationFutures which makes the service stateful; instead
remove those fields from the class and change the API so the owner supplies/owns
the caches (e.g., accept a Set<String> registeredExternalSignerPubkeys and
Map<String, Future<void>> externalSignerRegistrationFutures as constructor
parameters or as parameters on the methods that need them), keep
ExternalSignerCallbackRegistry as a stateless helper that only uses _enabled,
_getAccounts, and _registerSignerCallback, and update callers
(AuthNotifier/NotificationTaskHandler) to hold the caches and pass them into the
registry methods.

In `@lib/services/foreground_service.dart`:
- Around line 163-173: The current code swallows all errors from
_runEnsureExternalSigners() and continues to start subscriptions, which can race
if a required signer failed; change the flow so _runEnsureExternalSigners()
surfaces which pubkeys (or whether required pubkeys) failed and abort
subscription startup when any required signer registration failed: modify
_runEnsureExternalSigners() to throw or return a Result/failedPubkeys list on
critical failures, then in the caller (the block that currently calls
_runEnsureExternalSigners() before
_runEnsureSubscriptions()/ensureAllSubscriptions()) check that result and
return/throw instead of logging-and-continuting when required pubkeys are
missing; apply the same check-and-abort pattern to the other instance referenced
(the block around lines 197-203) so subscriptions never start if required signer
registrations failed.
- Around line 150-183: The _ensureSubscriptionRunning function can resume after
awaits even if ownership flips, causing a started subscription to be attached
when _shouldOwnSubscription is false; add a generation token or serializable
guard checked before and after each await (and immediately before calling
_startSubscription) to bail out if ownership changed, and make
_startSubscription/_stopSubscription respect that same token so they only
attach/detach the headless stream when the token matches; update checks in
_ensureSubscriptionRunning, _startSubscription, and _stopSubscription (and
mirror the same pattern for the similar block at lines 251-287) to serialize
start/stop and prevent resubscribe after yielding.

In `@test/services/foreground_service_test.dart`:
- Around line 46-56: The mock flips isRunning unconditionally in startService
and stopService which can hide failure-path bugs; update startService and
stopService so they only set isRunning = true when startResult indicates success
and only set isRunning = false when stopResult indicates success (use the mock's
startResult and stopResult values to decide), leaving isRunning unchanged on
failure; adjust assignments that reference lastServiceTypes/lastNotificationIcon
similarly only after a successful start.
```

issue.title: WnSystemNotice: 'Null check operator used on a null value' from auto-hide Timer firing after dispose
issue.body:
## Symptom

A user's logcat shows an unhandled Dart exception during a flow that surfaces a `WnSystemNotice` toast and then quickly transitions away from the screen:

\`\`\`
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/runtime/dart_vm_initializer.cc(40)]
                                Unhandled Exception: Null check operator used on a null value
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #0  AnimationController.stop
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:899)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #1  AnimationController._animateToInternal
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:673)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #2  AnimationController.reverse
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:521)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #3  WnSystemNotice.build.handleDismiss
                                    (package:whitenoise/widgets/wn_system_notice.dart:111)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #4  Timer._createTimer.<anonymous closure>
                                    (dart:async-patch/timer_patch.dart:18)
\`\`\`

It happened during a rapid sequence of three failed \"Add to group\" attempts (~3 s apart) where each surfaced an error toast and the user navigated between screens. The auto-hide Timer for a previous toast fired against a controller whose ticker had already been nulled out — `AnimationController.stop` reads `_ticker!` which throws when the controller has been disposed.

## Suspected cause

`lib/widgets/wn_system_notice.dart`:

\`\`\`dart
105    final autoHideTimer = useRef<Timer?>(null);
106
107    void handleDismiss() {
108      if (isDismissing.value) return;
109      isDismissing.value = true;
110      autoHideTimer.value?.cancel();
111      slideController.reverse().then((_) {        // <-- crash site
112        onDismiss?.call();
113      });
114    }

125    useEffect(() {
126      final duration = autoHideDuration ?? (_isTemporary ? _defaultAutoHideDuration : null);
127      if (duration != null && onDismiss != null) {
128        autoHideTimer.value = Timer(duration, handleDismiss);
129      }
130      return () => autoHideTimer.value?.cancel();
131    }, [autoHideDuration, _isTemporary, onDismiss]);
\`\`\`

The cleanup on line 130 cancels the Timer on dispose / dep change. But there is at least one window where the Timer has already fired and `handleDismiss` is queued (or running) before the cleanup runs — at that point `slideController.reverse()` executes against a disposed controller and `AnimationController.stop`'s `_ticker!` blows up.

There may also be a longer-running variant: `handleDismiss` fires *before* dispose, kicks off `slideController.reverse()`, and the widget is dismounted while the reverse animation is still ticking — same crash, different phase of the same bug.

## Suggested fix directions

1. **Guard `handleDismiss` against a disposed controller.** `AnimationController` has no public `isDisposed`, but we can capture a `mounted`-style flag with a `useRef<bool>` set to `false` in a cleanup, and bail out of `handleDismiss` if not mounted. (Or use the `useIsMounted` hook from `flutter_hooks` directly — that's exactly what it's for.)
2. **Don't capture a stale `handleDismiss`.** The Timer at line 128 captures the closure from the first build. A small refactor — extract `handleDismiss` into a `useCallback` and have the Timer invoke through a stable indirection — keeps the cancel/dismiss pair in sync across rebuilds.
3. **Wrap the `.then(...)` chain.** Even if everything else is correct, `slideController.reverse().then(...)` is exposing dispose-during-animation. Use `vsync`-aware navigation guards or check status before calling `onDismiss`.

The minimum fix is probably (1) — wrap the body of `handleDismiss` in an `if (!isMounted()) return;` check.

## Repro

Hard to reproduce deterministically; the captured trace happened during this sequence:

1. Trigger an action that surfaces a `WnSystemNotice` error toast (e.g., the failing add-to-group flow that produced the surrounding log entries).
2. Within ~3 s, navigate away from the screen so the parent widget is dismounted while the toast's auto-hide Timer is still pending or its dismiss animation is mid-flight.
3. The Timer fires into a disposed controller — unhandled exception.

A targeted test: mount a `WnSystemNotice` with `autoHideDuration: Duration(milliseconds: 50)`, pump 30 ms, dispose the host widget, then `pump(100)` — should reproduce.

## Severity

Doesn't crash the app but produces an unhandled exception in the Dart VM and — depending on how Flutter's error zone is configured — may or may not bubble to FlutterError. Easy fix, worth doing.

## Source

Caught in a real user's logcat during an unrelated investigation. Same log surfaced the `whitenoise-rs` `add_members` issue: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#813.

comment.body:
Again - I think this is intentional for the PR but it's very non-obvious looking at the code (in 6 months time) why this is set to do this. 

> After the initial load, `cache.hasLoaded` is `true`, so calling `refresh()` (which increments `manualRefreshKey`) never sets `isLoading` back to `true` during the async fetch. The caller (`_useChatList`) reads `blockedState.isLoading` to decide whether to suppress the chat list. This means after a block/unblock-triggered refresh, blocked content could be briefly visible while the new blocked-pubkeys list is still fetching, if the stream update and the async fetch race. This was the original behavior before caching, but the guard against it (`isLoading = true` at the top of the effect) has been weakened. Intentional or not, it should be explicit.

> The `useStream` return value is intentionally dropped — the hook drives rebuilds through the `useStream` side-effect, then reads from `cache.chatMap` directly. This is a valid pattern but it is non-obvious: a future reader will wonder why the snapshot is ignored. A short comment explaining the intent (`// useStream drives rebuilds; state lives in cache`) would be consistent with "really complex or hard to understand" exceptions in the style guide.
There are two of these in the file - another on line 488. It would be worth cleaning that up.

i think this is the intent of the PR - which is to show data when you go back and lazily make updates. BUT, I wanted to double check this. 

> When the user calls `refresh()`, `refreshKey` increments which re-subscribes to the stream, but `cache.hasInitialSnapshot` is never reset to `false`. This means `isLoading` stays `false` during the entire gap between the old subscription closing and the new `initialSnapshot` arriving. The visible effect is that after a manual refresh the list will briefly show the stale (pre-refresh) chats as if they were current, with no loading indicator to signal that data is being refreshed. Before this PR the old `ConnectionState.waiting` guard would naturally show the spinner during that window.
> 
> This may be acceptable if the intent is always "show cached, update lazily," but it would be worth an explicit decision and — if "stale is fine" — there should be a test that verifies the stale chats are shown (not hidden) during a refresh, so the contract is locked in.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In tokio::sync::broadcast, does RecvError::Lagged(_) mean messages were dropped irrecoverably for that receiver, requiring resubscription to regain consistency?`

💡 Result:

Yes—with an important nuance. RecvError::Lagged(u64) means that, for that particular receiver, the receiver fell so far behind that some earlier messages were no longer retained by the broadcast channel; the next recv will return the oldest message still retained by the channel, and the receiver is advanced to that oldest retained message [1]. Those skipped messages are gone for that receiver (dropped irrecoverably for it), but you generally do not need to resubscribe to “regain consistency”; you can just continue receiving after handling Lagged, since the receiver position is updated [1][2]. The docs explicitly describe this as detecting that data was dropped and say the caller may either abort its task or tolerate lost messages and resume consuming the channel [2]. So: Lagged implies lost messages for that receiver are irrecoverable, but recovery in the sense of getting back in sync usually just means continuing recv (the receiver is repositioned), not calling subscribe again [1][2].

Citations:

- 1: https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/broadcast/error/enum.RecvError.html
- 2: https://rustdocs.bsx.fi/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html

---

🏁 Script executed:

```shell
fd -t f group_state.rs
```

Repository: marmot-protocol/whitenoise

Length of output: 98

---

🏁 Script executed:

```shell
cat -n rust/src/api/group_state.rs
```

Repository: marmot-protocol/whitenoise

Length of output: 3879

---



</details>

**Treat lag as terminal in this transition-only stream.**

At Line 65, `RecvError::Lagged(_)` is ignored with `continue`. This stream is documented as transition-only with no snapshot, emitting only two possible terminal states: `LeftGroup` or `RemovedFromGroup`. If either of these events is dropped due to lag, the event is lost irrecoverably and the Dart side remains desynchronized—continuing recv will not re-emit it. Close the stream on lag so callers can resubscribe and reconcile membership state.

> 🤖 **[suggestion]** `_subscriptionRunning` (new field) and `_subscription != null` (pre-existing pattern in `_startSubscription`) track the same concept through different code paths. `ensureSubscriptionRunning()` checks `_subscriptionRunning`, while `_startSubscription()` returns early based on `_subscription != null`. If these ever diverge (e.g., the stream closes unexpectedly while `_subscriptionRunning` stays `true`), the `onRepeatEvent` health check becomes a no-op and the subscription never recovers.
> 
> **How to address:** Collapse to one source of truth. `_subscriptionRunning` could be derived from `_subscription?.isRunning ?? false` (since `NotificationSubscription` already exposes `isRunning`), or remove `_subscriptionRunning` entirely and let `_startSubscription`'s `_subscription != null` check be the idempotency guard.

My agent dissagrees with me a bit in the argument for having them joined in one service, but aggrees in the naming confusion. 

> 🤖 The new `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` is a lifecycle orchestrator layered on top of it. The split is technically legitimate:
> 
> - `AndroidSignerService` = NIP-55 wire protocol (sign event, encrypt, decrypt, `registerExternalSigner`)
> - `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` = decides *when* and *for which accounts* to call `registerExternalSigner`, with deduplication and multi-account coordination
> 
> However, the naming causes real confusion. `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` sounds like it could be absorbed into `AndroidSignerService`, especially since `AndroidSignerService.registerExternalSigner` already exists and the new service's only non-trivial responsibility is deduplication and reconciliation logic. The conceptual split is defensible but the naming makes it look like unnecessary proliferation.

My agent raised a point here too and I think it makes sense: this service by its name seems to be  more generic than just for android signers, but then it defaults to AndroidSignerService which is confusing without having a platform check when used... ) 

This is the original comment my agent left:

> **🤖 [must]** The service hardcodes `AndroidSignerService().registerExternalSigner` as its default with no platform guard. `AndroidSignerService` is Android-only. On iOS, `AccountType.external_` should never exist (iOS users can't log in via Amber), but this is an **implicit invariant, not an enforced one**. If a corrupted or cross-platform data store somehow produced an `external_` account on iOS, this service would attempt to invoke the Android plugin.
> 
> `AndroidSignerService.registerExternalSigner` itself also does NOT check `Platform.isAndroid` before calling `signer_api.registerExternalSigner` — so the platform check would cascade all the way to a Rust FFI call with unregistered Android callbacks.

My agent dissagrees with me and does not think this is a real issue. Let's wait for pepi's QA review though

`### 🤖 Is the non-external signer case handled correctly?

**Yes, correctly handled at two defensive layers:**

1. In `reconcile()`: filters to `account.accountType == AccountType.external_` before building the map — local accounts never enter the registration path.
2. In `_registerExternalSignerIfMissing()`: explicit early return `if (account.accountType != accounts_api.AccountType.external_) return`.

A local account that happens to have Amber installed will never trigger external signer registration. The test `'does not re-register for local account'` (existing) and `'re-registers inactive external signer accounts'` (new, mixed local+external scenario) both verify this correctly.`

I personally try to avoid using visible for testing approach. 

> 🤖 Avoid @visibleForTesting — tests that reach internal methods break on harmless refactors and can hit full coverage while the public interface is broken. Use it only when the behavior is impossible to exercise otherwise.
I see that this condition was moved inside of  complete login , but `_ensureExternalSignersRegistered `is still called here

I feel it is confusing to have 2 services now related to external signers (`AndroidSignerService ` and this new one` ExternalSignerRegistration`).  I think that if all logic is related to an External signer it would be simpler to have all this methods grouped under a single service. WDYT?

Why the condition to check if an account was external or not was removed?

`if (account.accountType == accounts_api.AccountType.external_) `

 This might be problematic for accounts created with login with nsec in devices where amber is present and used but for other accounts. Unless I'm missing something.
When this case could happen? that seems to me like an invalid pubkey...

This is for me super confusing to read. So the service in charge of registering an external signer need to receive the method to register it? So the other service is in part in charge too of registering a signer. That makes me think that this 2 should just live together in a single service as I mentioned above.

issue.title: fix: preserve chat list state across screen remounts (#483)
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/f3757fc28c0f4949a066f4338316f1d54ce148f70322d769352aa5b94cafb459.png) Closes #483. Returning to the chat list flashed a loading spinner because go_router's `goNamed` disposes `ChatListScreen`, and on pop the `useChatList` hook re-subscribed to the stream with no cached data. So every back-navigation looked like a cold start. Cache the chat-list map (per pubkey + archived) and the blocked-pubkeys set (per pubkey) at module scope so they outlive widget disposal. `isLoading` now gates on whether an initial snapshot was ever received, not on the current stream's connection state. A remount renders the cached marmots immediately and updates lazily as new stream events arrive. Regression test in `test/hooks/use_chat_list_test.dart` reproduces the bug (fails on old code, passes on the fix). Screen-level test in `test/screens/chat_list_screen_test.dart` locks in the user-flow behavior. Test-side cache reset is wired into `MockWnApi.reset()` so individual test files keep their existing setUp. `just precommit` passes. Coverage 99.36%. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Chat data now persists when navigating back to the chat list from an individual conversation, eliminating unnecessary loading states. * Implemented session-based caching for chat lists and blocked contacts to prevent redundant network requests, improving navigation speed and reducing data usage.

issue.body:
## Status

A first version of this feature **already shipped on 2026-03-20** via PR #506 (closes #505). This issue tracks the gaps that remain.

## What shipped in #506

- Rust API `fetch_latest_zapstore_version()` queries `relay.zapstore.dev` for the kind:32267 software application event for `org.parres.whitenoise`, follows the `a` tag to the kind:30063 release, and returns the version string.
- Flutter hook `useZapstoreUpdate` runs **on app start only** on Android, compares against installed `PackageInfo.version` using CalVer segment comparison.
- Dismissible info banner on the chat list with an "Update now" button that opens the Zapstore listing via `url_launcher`.
- Localized in 8 languages.

## What's still missing

The shipped version is the minimum viable banner. The following deltas still need work:

### 1. Publisher pubkey pinning (security)

`fetch_latest_zapstore_version()` queries kind:32267 by `d` tag (`org.parres.whitenoise`) without an `authors:` filter for the official White Noise publisher pubkey. Any Nostr key can publish a kind:32267 with the same `d` tag. If a malicious or compromised relay returns a spoofed event, the app will compare against an attacker-controlled version string.

**Fix**: hardcode the official White Noise publisher pubkey in the app and add it to the `authors:` filter on both kind:32267 and kind:30063 queries. Drop any event whose signature does not match.

This is the load-bearing security primitive for everything else here — until it lands, none of the items below should be expanded.

### 2. Periodic polling

Currently the check fires once per app start. A user who keeps the app open for days never re-checks.

**Proposal**: re-poll every 24 hours while the app is running, in addition to app start. Cache the latest seen version locally so we don't re-banner on the same release.

### 3. Escalation when far behind

The banner is uniformly dismissible regardless of how stale the build is. A user 5 releases behind sees the same low-key banner as someone 1 release behind.

**Proposal**:
- 0–2 releases behind: current dismissible banner (no change)
- 3+ releases behind: persistent, harder-to-dismiss banner with stronger copy. Re-show on every cold start until updated. The user is running a build that may be incompatible with the network — see #610 for an example of a backward-compat break across versions.

This requires knowing how many releases the user is behind, which requires either fetching the full `30063` release history or having Zapstore expose a counter. Implementation detail to be decided.

### 4. OS-level notification when backgrounded

The banner only shows once the user opens the app. If they haven't opened it in a week, they don't see anything.

**Proposal**: when the periodic poll fires and detects a new release, post a system notification (subject to the existing notification permission). Tapping it opens the chat list with the banner shown.

### 5. Settings row showing installed vs. latest

A user who dismisses the banner has no way to find their version-status again without checking Zapstore externally.

**Proposal**: add a row in Settings showing installed version, latest version, and how many releases behind. Tapping opens Zapstore. This is also a useful diagnostic field for support reports.

## iOS scope

iOS remains out of scope for the same reasons documented in the original issue:
- App Store: app updates are automatic by default. When users disable auto-update, the App Store notifies them. https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT202180
- TestFlight: the TestFlight app surfaces beta updates and supports automatic updates per build group. https://developer.apple.com/testflight/

Not tested on iOS — verification was via Apple's published documentation only.

## Test platform

GrapheneOS. All notification additions must respect the hardened permission model.

## Cross-reference

- Original problem statement: #505 (closed)
- First implementation: PR #506 (merged 2026-03-20)
- Auto-update follow-up: #622

issue.title: Dismiss chat list search on swipe-back instead of closing app
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/3dbf71efd665c3c69001188af6b8d1dd8d18f6a4ae803d11851488397070d5d9.png) On Android (e.g. GrapheneOS), the swipe-back gesture used to evict the entire app even when the chat list search bar was open. Wrong target: back should dismiss in-screen state first. The fix wraps `ChatListScreen` in a `PopScope` that intercepts the gesture whenever the search header is revealed or the query field has text. On intercept it unfocuses the keyboard, clears the query, and collapses the header. Once search is no longer visible, back falls through to its normal route pop. To enable parent-driven dismissal, `WnChatList` now accepts an optional `headerOpenNotifier`. When provided, the screen owns the open/closed state and a `useEffect` inside `WnChatList` animates the reveal in response to external changes. Callers without the notifier keep the previous internal state. Tested with three new widget tests covering: header dismissal on back, query clear on back, and pass-through when no search is active. Coverage holds at 99.33%. The marmots wave goodbye to the search bar, not to the whole burrow. Closes #612 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved back button behavior when search UI is active. Back button now closes the search header instead of exiting the entire screen, then closes the app on subsequent press. * Enhanced header visibility synchronization with improved animation control. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive test coverage for back navigation behavior with active search. * Added tests for header visibility control and scroll position management.

issue.title: fix: close bug report screen with success snackbar after submission
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c559b29941fec25c2aa57a0b412dddc57bf120a0431e1926624aca559a21aa0e.jpg) Closes #627 ## What was wrong After tapping Send on a bug report, the screen stayed open with the text intact. # Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

**Actionable comments posted: 2**

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@lib/hooks/use_leave_group.dart`:
- Around line 105-108: The current sequence in use_leave_group.dart calls
groups_api.selfDemote(...) then groups_api.leaveGroup(...), which can leave a
user demoted if the second call fails; change this to a single atomic operation
by adding and calling a combined bridge/Rust method (e.g.,
groups_api.demoteAndLeave(pubkey: accountPubkey, groupId: groupId)) that
performs both actions in one transaction, or if you cannot add a bridge change
immediately, implement an explicit rollback: call selfDemote only after a
successful leaveGroup or, if you must demote first, catch leaveGroup failures
and call groups_api.selfPromote(...) to restore admin rights (use isAdmin,
accountPubkey, groupId to locate state), and surface errors so callers know the
operation did not complete atomically.
- Around line 53-69: The current Future.wait groups_api.groupRequiredProposals
and groups_api.groupAdmins calls tie their failures together causing any
admin-fetch error to reset hasNostrCapabilities; change the logic in the hook so
you call groups_api.groupRequiredProposals(...) and groups_api.groupAdmins(...)
independently (separate awaits or try/catch blocks), set
hasNostrCapabilities.value based only on the result of groupRequiredProposals
(checking for RequiredProposal.selfRemove), and set adminPubkeys.value only from
the groupAdmins result; on errors, handle each failure separately (e.g., log the
error and leave the other state unchanged or set a distinct admin-fetch error
state) so admin fetch failures no longer flip hasNostrCapabilities.
```
